q: 1. Maximum bending moment in a beam occurs where
explain: Since dM/dx = Shear Force, the bending moment is maximum (or minimum) where the shear force is zero, i.e. where the SF diagram changes sign.

q: 2. Rate of change of bending moment is equal to
explain: From beam theory, dM/dx = V (Shear Force); hence rate of change of bending moment along the span equals the shear force at that section.

q: 3. The product EI is called
explain: The product of Young's modulus (E) and Moment of Inertia (I) defines the bending resistance of a beam, known as flexural rigidity.

q: 4. In a continuous bending moment curve he point where it changes sign, is called
explain: All three terms — point of inflexion, point of contraflexure, and point of virtual hinge — refer to the same location where the bending moment changes sign (crosses zero).

q: 5. The shear force on a simply supported beam is proportional to
options: algebraic sum of the transverse forces of the section
explain: Shear force at a section is defined as the algebraic sum of all transverse forces acting on one side of that section (signs matter for direction).

q: 6. A reinforced concrete beam is assumed to be made of
explain: RCC combines two different materials (concrete and steel) with different properties, so it is treated as a heterogeneous (composite) material in analysis.

q: 7. Stress in a beam due to simple bending is
explain: Bending stress is directly proportional to the distance from the neutral axis (y).

q: 8. The deflection of a uniform circular bar of diameter d and length l, which extends by an amount e under a tensile pull W, when it carries the same load at its mid span is
explain: Comparing the bending deflection (from flexure formula) to the axial elongation e of the same circular bar under the same load W gives a deflection expression proportional to e²l/3d², matching option (c).

q: 9. A cantilever of length L is subjected to a bending moment M at its free end. If EI is the flexural rigidity of the section, the deflection of the free end is
explain: For a cantilever under a pure end moment M, standard deflection formula gives free-end deflection = ML²/2EI.

q: 10. A portion of beam between two sections is said to be in pure bending when there is
options: constant bending moment and zero shear force
constant shear force and zero bending moment
constant bending moment and constant shear force
explain: Pure bending occurs over a beam segment where the bending moment is constant and the shear force is zero (since dM/dx = V = 0 implies M is constant).

q: 11. A rectangular beam carries a maximum bending moment of M. If its depth is doubled, its moment carrying capacity will be
explain: Moment capacity is proportional to the Section Modulus Z (BD²/6). If D is doubled (2D), Z becomes B(2D)²/6 = 4BD²/6, increasing capacity 4 times.

q: 12. A prismatic bar when subjected to pure bending assumes the shape of
explain: Under pure (constant) bending moment, curvature 1/R = M/EI is constant, so the beam bends into a circular arc.

q: 13. The shear force and bending moment are related by
explain: The rate of change of the bending moment (dM/dx) at any section is equal to the shear force (V) at that section.

q: 14. Which one is correct if the deflection of a beam is y
explain: The slope (θ) of a beam's elastic curve is the first derivative of the deflection (y) with respect to x.

q: 15. The maximum deflection in the cantilever beam subjected to an udl of W /m throughout the span is
explain: This is a standard deflection formula for a cantilever beam under a uniformly distributed load.

q: 16. A simply supported beam of length l carries a load varying uniformly from zero at left end to maximum at right end maximum bending moment occurs at a distance of
explain: For a triangular load, the maximum moment occurs where shear force is zero, which is at a distance of l/√3 from the apex (zero load end).

q: 17. Load carrying capacity of fixed beam is
options: greater than simply supported beam and cantilever beam
explain: A fixed beam has a higher degree of redundancy and smaller maximum bending moments compared to simply supported or cantilever beams for the same span and loading, allowing it to carry more load.

q: 18. At either ends of plane frame, maximum number of possible bending moment, are
explain: According to the provided answer key, the value is zero; this typically refers to idealized hinged or pinned connections at the ends of a frame where no moment is transferred.

q: 19. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, having no external load is
explain: When there is no external load (only point loads or moments at ends), the shear force is constant and the bending moment varies linearly.

q: 20. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly distributed load is
explain: The bending moment is the integral of the shear force. For a UDL, the shear force is linear, so the bending moment diagram follows a second-degree (parabolic) curve.

q: 21. In any beam, there is acting uniformly moment then its curve is
explain: The key indicates 'parabolic arch', though pure bending (constant moment) typically results in a circular elastic curve; however, in the context of load diagrams, 'parabolic' is often associated with distributed forces.

q: 22. For a simply supported beam with a central load, the bending moment is
explain: With a central point load, the bending moment increases linearly from zero at the supports to a maximum value of WL/4 at the center.

q: 23. For a cantilever with a uniformly distributed load, w over its entire length L, the maximum bending moment is
explain: The total load is wL acting at a distance L/2 from the fixed support. Thus, M = (wL) * (L/2) = wL²/2 at the fixed end.

q: 24. In a cantilever beam a point load is applied at the free end. Which one is correct?
options: SF is uniform throughout the beam
SF varies linearly from free end to fixed end
BM is uniform throughout the beam
explain: Since there is only one load at the end and no other loads, the shear force remains constant (uniform) at value W across the entire length.

q: 25. The moment diagram for a cantilever carrying concentrated load at its free end will be
explain: The moment varies linearly from 0 at the free end to WL at the fixed end, creating a triangular shape.

q: 26. Shear force for a cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load over its whole length is
explain: The shear force varies linearly from 0 at the free end to wL at the fixed end, resulting in a triangular Shear Force Diagram.

q: 27. The influence line diagram for BM at a section in a cantilever will be a triangle extending between the section and the
options: fixed end with maximum ordinate under the section
fixed end with maximum ordinate under the fixed end
unsupported end with maximum ordinate at the section
unsupported end with maximum ordinate at the supported end
explain: The bending moment at a section is created by the load multiplied by its distance from that section. The maximum moment occurs when the unit load is at the farthest possible point from the support (the free/unsupported end).

q: 28. A beam is a structural member predominantly subjected to
explain: A beam, by definition, is a structural member designed to primarily resist transverse (perpendicular to its axis) loads, developing shear and bending.

q: 29. In general equation for the deflection of the beam: M=EI*  where EI is
explain: EI represent the flexural strength.

q: 30. A rigid frame is a structure composed of members which are connected by
explain: By definition, a rigid frame has members connected by rigid (moment-resisting) joints, as opposed to pin-jointed trusses.

q: 31. When the load does not pass through the shear centre of the steel beam. It produces
options: torsional moment along with bending moment
explain: Loads not passing through the shear center cause twisting (torsion). The resistance to this is related to the torsional and sectional rigidity of the beam.

q: 32. When a cantilever beam of length l is loaded with a uniformly varying load of maximum intensity w at free end, the shape of bending moment diagram is
explain: Since the load is linear (varying), the shear force is parabolic ($x^2$), and the bending moment is a cubic function ($x^3$).

q: 33. Prestressing to a large extent removes the disadvantages which a conventional reinforced concrete structure suffers as compared to a comparable :
explain: Prestressing allows concrete to span longer distances and remain crack-free, making it competitive with steel structures.

q: 34. A one dimensional structure is one in which
options: one dimension is very small and other two are large
one dimension is much larger than the other two dimensions
all the three dimensions are equal
explain: A one-dimensional structure (like a beam or column) has its length dimension much larger than its cross-sectional dimensions.

q: 35. A two dimensional structure is one in which
options: two dimensions are very much larger than the third
two dimensions are very much smaller than the third
explain: A two-dimensional structure (like a slab or wall) has two dimensions (length and width) much larger than the third (thickness).

q: 36. The point of contraflexure occurs in
explain: Overhanging beams typically have both sagging (within supports) and hogging (over the overhang) moments, so the bending moment changes sign, creating a point of contraflexure.

q: 37. A beam of T-section is subjected to a shear force of F. The maximum shear force will occur at the
explain: As with most sections, the maximum shear stress in a T-section occurs at the neutral axis, where the parabolic shear distribution peaks within the web.

q: 38. A rectangular beam of length l supported at its two ends carries a central point load W. The maximum deflection occurs
explain: For a simply supported beam under a symmetric central point load, maximum deflection (by symmetry) occurs exactly at the midspan (centre).

q: 39. If he shear force long a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is
explain: Since dM/dx = Shear Force, a zero shear force at a section indicates the bending moment is at a local extreme (maximum or minimum) at that point.

q: 40. A cantilever beam rectangular in cross-section is subjected to an isolated load at its free end. If the width of the beam is doubled, the deflection of the free end will be changed in the ratio of
explain: Since deflection δ ∝ 1/I and I ∝ b (width) for a rectangular section, doubling the width halves the deflection.

q: 41. The ratio of the maximum deflections of a simply supported beam with a central load W and of a cantilever of same length and with a load W at its free end is
explain: Comparing WL³/48EI (simply supported, central load) to WL³/3EI (cantilever, end load) gives a ratio of (1/48)/(1/3) = 1/16.

q: 42. In a rigid jointed frame, the joints are considered
options: to rotate only as a whole
that 50% of members rotate in clockwise direction and 50% in anti clockwise direction
explain: At a rigid joint, all connected members are assumed to rotate together by the same angle (the joint rotates as a whole, maintaining the rigid angles between members).

q: 43. For a beam of uniform strength, if depth is constant
explain: For a rectangular section with constant depth d, since σ ∝ M/(bd²), keeping stress constant with fixed d requires width b to vary directly proportional to M.

q: 44. In the case of H section the maximum shear stress will occur at
options: at the junction of the web and flanges
explain: For an H-section (similar to I-section), there's a notable jump in shear stress at the web-flange junction due to the abrupt change in width, often making this location critical.

q: 45. The maximum deflection due to uniformly distributed load w per unit length over entire span of a cantilever of length l and of flexural rigidity EI is
explain: The standard formula for maximum (tip) deflection of a cantilever under UDL over its full length is wl⁴/8EI.

q: 46. The ratio of the deflections of the free end of a cantilever due to an isolated load at 1/3rd and 2/3rd of the span is
explain: Using the standard cantilever deflection formula for a load at distance a from the fixed end (deflection at tip involves a²(3L-a)), evaluating for a=L/3 versus a=2L/3 and taking the ratio gives 2/7.

q: 47. The moment diagram for a cantilever which is subjected to a uniformly distributed load will be a
explain: For a cantilever under UDL, the bending moment varies quadratically (parabolically) along its length, being zero at the free end and maximum at the fixed end.
